blocks.content: Quiz: Why does useSearch() accept entries as a parameter instead of fetching them itself?
Tap an option below to answer:
Because each hook should do only one thing
A hook that both fetches and filters would be tightly coupled and hard to reuse. useSearch() filters, useFetch() fetches, and they compose together in App.
A hook that both fetches and filters would be tightly coupled and hard to reuse. useSearch() filters, useFetch() fetches, and they compose together in App.
Because hooks cannot call other hooks
Custom hooks can absolutely call other hooks. That is how they are composed.
Custom hooks can absolutely call other hooks. That is how they are composed.
Because filtering requires the URL, not the entries array
Filtering only needs the data. It doesn't care where the data came from.
Filtering only needs the data. It doesn't care where the data came from.
Because useMemo() cannot run inside a custom hook
useMemo() works anywhere hooks are allowed, including inside custom hooks.
useMemo() works anywhere hooks are allowed, including inside custom hooks.
